To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of lexical markers can activate social identity and influence intergroup perception.

(1) the use of social lexical markers in a text has an impact on the perception of intergroup relations; (2) this effect is more marked when the marker is used in the context of an out group, than in the context of the in group; and (3) this effect is not due to a simple in group bias.
social lexical markers are a clue for social identity and intergroup relations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interplay of linguistic and social factors.
the interplay of language use and social identities.
the interplay of language and social identity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lexical markers are a powerful tool to activate the social identity and to influence the attitude toward the out group, and that this influence depends on the social identity activation type.
language use is a social clue, and social identity activation can have an impact on intergroup perception.
language use is not neutral and can be used to influence intergroup relations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the lexical markers used by the leaders of the two opposed groups are not only a social clue, but they also have a social influence on the members of these groups.
language is a clue of social identity, and that it is a clue that can be manipulated to change attitudes and intergroup perceptions. (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2019 APA, all rights reserved)
the language used in communication has an impact on the social perception of intergroup relations and that this impact depends on the lexical markers used.
The main takeaway from our work is that
language is a social clue, a tool to convey social information.
social identity can be activated by language use, and this activation is a key factor in the intergroup perception.
language is an essential social cue that can influence social perception and attitude.
